# Nigeria Tops Africa Startup Funding at $635M [2026]
![Laura Bennett](https://shattered.io/wp-content/uploads/avatars/lbennett.webp)

[Laura Bennett](https://shattered.io/author/lbennett/)

Updated Oct 23, 2026 · 17 min read

![Nigeria Tops Africa Startup Funding at $635M](https://shattered.io/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/nigeria-tops-africa-startup-funding-635-million-2026-gen-1024x585.webp)

Nigerian startups raised **$635 million** between January and September 2026, according to data from the tracker Africa: The Big Deal, and that total puts Nigeria back at the top of the continent’s startup-funding table. [BusinessDay reported](https://businessday.ng/technology/article/nigeria-reclaims-africas-startup-funding-lead-as-investment-hits-635m/) that the result is Nigeria’s first lead in African startup funding since 2022. Reports published on October 21 put the figure at 2.6 times the $247 million Nigerian startups raised in the same nine months of 2025.

The deal count rose too, though far less sharply. A total of 77 Nigerian ventures raised funding in the period, up from 70 a year earlier. That gap between a 157% jump in dollars and a 10% rise in deals tells most of the story, because a handful of very large rounds carried the headline number.

Capital is flowing to emerging-market founders well beyond Lagos, as a recent [$300K pre-seed for a Saudi event-tech startup](https://shattered.io/inve-saudi-event-tech-300k-pre-seed-outliers-vc-2026/) showed. Still, Nigeria startup funding is now the clearest signal of where African software demand is heading.

## Egypt Closes In: $445 Million in Second Place
| Group (Jan-Sep 2026) | Amount raised | Share of Africa total (derived) |
|-|-|-|
| All African startups | about $2.16 billion | 100% |
| Nigeria | $635 million | about 29.4% |
| Egypt | $445 million | about 20.6% |
| Nigeria and Egypt combined | $1.08 billion | 50.0% |
| Moove, Flutterwave, Jumia, Yellow Card combined | $440 million | about 20.4% |
| Rest of Nigeria (73 ventures) | about $195 million | about 9.0% |
| All other markets and pan-African ventures | about $1.08 billion | 50.0% |

## Africa’s $2.16 Billion Total and the Wider Funding Climate
African startups collectively raised approximately **$2.16 billion** between January and September 2026.

Compare Nigeria’s total with the [$90 million seed round for a robot foundation-model startup](https://shattered.io/dream-labs-90m-seed-robot-foundation-model-2026/), which by itself represents about 14% of everything Nigerian startups raised in nine months.

The country drew a total that beats its own prior-year number by 157%, even though the continental total is far smaller than the headline AI rounds elsewhere. [Business AM](https://businessamlive.com/nigeria-leads-africa-startup-funding-race-with-635m-in-nine-months/) and [MSME Africa](https://msmeafricaonline.com/nigerian-startups-raise-635m-in-nine-months-lead-africas-funding-market/) both led their coverage with the leadership angle, and The Whistler pointed to the inflow figure instead.

## Five Predictions for Late 2026 and 2027
4. **Compliance and security tooling will grow fastest.** Regulated fintech and crypto businesses cannot scale without audit-ready systems.

## FAQ: Nigeria Startup Funding in 2026
### How does that compare with 2025?
The 2026 total is 2.6 times the $247 million raised in the same period of 2025. The number of ventures raising at least $100,000 rose from 70 to 77.

### Which companies raised the most?
Moove, Flutterwave, Jumia and Yellow Card together raised $440 million, about 69% of Nigeria’s total. The available reports do not give a confirmed amount for each company individually.

### How much did all of Africa raise?
African startups collectively raised approximately $2.16 billion between January and September 2026. Nigeria and Egypt together account for $1.08 billion, or half of that total.

### What does Africa: The Big Deal track?
The tracker monitors African startups that raise at least $100,000.
